claim_boundary: Source audit of known native trace coverage, not a dynamic completeness test. A note site demonstrates instrumentation code exists, not that every caller path or all access classes are covered.

findings.family: interpreted and selected JIT node reads

coverage: NodesWhere indexed/fallback query markers and rows
NodesOfType returned rows (population scan not explicitly marked)
findings.detail: NodesWhere records a query marker for both indexed and fallback paths and distinguishes scanned candidates from returned rows. NodesOfType currently records only returned-node type reads; an empty result has no query event, and scanned population size must be obtained from separate work accounting.

findings.limit: The event is emitted after a binding succeeds; a 1-versus-9 candidate probe showed cand_tested scaling 1-to-9 while successful pattern_edge events stayed at 1. Predicate attribute reads were traced for all candidates, but rejected candidate edge identities and scheduler/index work were not fully represented.

coverage: node type and attribute fingerprint reads under an active RuleUid
partial decoder reads on cache misses
findings.detail: sd_cache_key now emits a typed-population query marker and note_node_type_and_attrs for every fingerprinted node, so key-construction reads are visible on both cache hits and misses under an active RuleUid. Direct evaluations without a RuleUid remain unattributed, and the trace does not label hit versus miss. A paired 1-versus-2 computed-effect probe observed exactly 2-versus-4 query markers per type with semantic parity.
findings.family: shape-decode cache fingerprint and decoder scans

findings.detail: UseTool evaluates arguments and calls the registered Python handler; callback reads, writes, and external side effects are not represented as native graph-access events. A paired probe independently observed one callback invocation in both traced/untraced arms and no tool-kind trace row.

SetAttrIfDifferent reads the old value before deciding whether it writes; current events record the effect write only on the changed branch, not a separate concrete old-value read. A paired probe confirmed unchanged and changed arms preserve semantics, while only the changed arm emits the target write event. Static writesets remain a separate diagnostic.

note() returns without recording when the thread-local current rule UID is zero. Adapter work, post-rule queue draining, and other operations outside an entered rule are therefore invisible to this event stream.
findings.family: host/scheduler work outside a rule UID

next_probe: Attribute trace work outside active RuleUID/scope pairs, post-rule queued effects, and host callbacks; calibrate scheduler and matcher counters against those event sites. Failed-candidate, SetAttrIfDifferent, and UseTool omissions have bounded probes, but no complete dynamic trace-recall estimate exists. Cache hit/miss labels may aid attribution but do not close these omissions.
